Verified pinned backend context for this phase:

- desktop.Window.Lock is the composer ownership mutex w.Mu (patch 0016 rechecks teardown after taking it). core.renderWindow.renderAsyncOwned takes this window mutex before Compose. The fast resize Redraw path takes the same mutex before Redraw.
- gpudraw.Drawer.drawAll calls BeginRenderPass, submits via EndRenderPass, then presents within that already-owned window batch. Surface.GetCurrentTexture takes sf.Mutex, retained until Present releases it. Neither surface acquire/configure/present nor GPU submission acquires a window or renderContext mutex.
- desktop.Window.updateGeometry takes w.Mu before Renderer.SetSize. Its lock order is window then surface. Async composition is renderContext then window then surface. The surface code has no reverse dependency. Moving native surface reconfiguration outside w.Mu reproduced a live validation failure by invalidating an acquired presentation texture before submission.
- Surface.Config itself does not acquire sf.Mutex; Reconfig does. The bounded acquire retry receives Config while already holding sf.Mutex.
- The acquired base surface texture reference must survive submission and presentation; its view alone did not prevent the actual backend from reporting destroyed Surface Texture. Both are released after surface.Present.

These facts provide cross-file context, without severity overrides or exclusions.

Verified canvas call graph: core.WidgetBase.RenderWidget invokes canvasWidget.Render during scene update/layout/render, before core.renderWindow takes SystemWindow.Lock to gather composer sources. Composition invokes xyzcore.xyzSource.Draw, which only locks XYZ and reads the current frame; it never calls canvasWidget.Render or Application.Do. Resource APIs are called on the UI owner without already holding a native window lock. Native teardown withdraws composerPointer before DestroyGPUFunc, so canvas Destroy does not reacquire a window being destroyed. The race-instrumented live smoke covers render, rebuild, snapshot, resize, minimize/restore and destruction without deadlock.
